## GWAS Variant Annotation

```{r variant-annotation-setup}
# Genome reference: Affymetrix SNP Array 6.0, GRCh37/hg19

# Install once if needed:
# BiocManager::install(c("VariantAnnotation",
#                        "TxDb.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg19.knownGene",
#                        "org.Hs.eg.db"))

rm(list = ls())

# Libraries
library(dplyr)
library(VariantAnnotation)
library(TxDb.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg19.knownGene)
library(org.Hs.eg.db)
library(gt)

setwd("/Users/dubsirubs/universidad/estadistica/gwas/")

# Load saved objects
load("lab3_save.RData")

source("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CrisVanHout-LIIGH/Class/refs/heads/main/LabFunctions.R")

# Load and annotate GWAS results
# Note: if merge runs out of memory see https://stackoverflow.com/questions/51295402/r-on-macos-error-vector-memory-exhausted-limit-reached
GWASout <- read.table("GWAA.txt", header = TRUE,
                      colClasses = c("character", rep("numeric", 4)))
colnames(GWASout) <- c("SNP", "effect", "stdErr", "tValue", "pValue")
GWASout$Neg_logP  <- -log10(GWASout$pValue)
GWASout <- merge(GWASout, genoMap[, c("SNP", "chr", "position", "A1", "A2")], by = "SNP")
GWASout$MAF <- snpsum.col[GWASout$SNP, "MAF"]
GWASout <- arrange(GWASout, -Neg_logP)
```

## Top-Hit Annotation

```{r top-hit-annotation}
N       <- 10
topHits <- GWASout[order(GWASout$pValue), ][1:N, ]

# Build GRanges for top hits
targets <- with(topHits,
                GRanges(seqnames = Rle(paste0("chr", chr)),
                        ranges   = IRanges(position, end = position, names = SNP),
                        strand   = Rle("*")))

# Locate variants relative to UCSC known genes
loc       <- locateVariants(targets, TxDb.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg19.knownGene, AllVariants())
out       <- as.data.frame(loc, row.names = NULL)
out$names <- names(targets)[out$QUERYID]
out       <- unique(out[, c("names", "seqnames", "start", "end", "LOCATION", "GENEID")])

# Convert Entrez IDs to gene symbols via AnnotationDbi
# Note: keep gene symbols out of Excel (auto-converts e.g. MARCH1 to dates)
entrezIDs    <- unique(na.omit(as.character(out$GENEID)))
symbolMap    <- AnnotationDbi::select(org.Hs.eg.db,
                                      keys    = entrezIDs,
                                      columns = "SYMBOL",
                                      keytype = "ENTREZID")
out$GENESYMBOL <- symbolMap$SYMBOL[match(as.character(out$GENEID), symbolMap$ENTREZID)]

# Merge annotation back to top hits
# all.x = TRUE preserves SNPs with no gene overlap; duplicates arise for multi-gene loci
annotatedHits <- merge(topHits, out, by.x = "SNP", by.y = "names", all.x = TRUE)
annotatedHits <- dplyr::select(annotatedHits, -any_of(c("start", "tValue", "Neg_logP",
                                                 "seqnames", "GENEID", "end")))
annotatedHits <- annotatedHits[, c("SNP", "chr", "position", "A1", "A2", "MAF",
                                   "effect", "stdErr", "pValue",
                                   "LOCATION", "GENESYMBOL")]
annotatedHits <- arrange(annotatedHits, pValue)

# Display formatted table
# Effect sizes are per copy of allele 2 (A2), the allele counted by the GWAS; MAF is the frequency of the less common allele
# Reference: Table 1 style from https://www.nature.com/articles/ng.2797
annotatedHits %>%
  gt() %>%
  tab_header(
    title    = "Top GWAS Hits",
    subtitle = "Annotated with gene symbols and genomic position"
  ) %>%
  fmt_number(columns = c(effect, stdErr, MAF), decimals = 3) %>%
  fmt_scientific(columns = pValue, decimals = 2) %>%
  cols_label(
    SNP        = "rsID",
    chr        = "Chromosome",
    position   = "Position",
    A1         = "Allele 1",
    A2         = "Allele 2",
    MAF        = "MAF",
    effect     = "Effect per A2 Copy",
    stdErr     = "Std. Error",
    pValue     = "P-value",
    LOCATION   = "Location",
    GENESYMBOL = "Gene Symbol"
  ) %>%
  tab_options(table.font.size = 12, heading.align = "center")
```

### Use of AI-Assisted Tools

AI-assisted tools were used to support the documentation of the laboratory, improve the clarity of written explanations, and address questions related to statistical concepts and R code. The tools served as supplementary assistance during the development and review of the work.
